record.original_question: Let M be an arbitrary finite set of strings. Extend the notion of the degree of randomness of a string x, which compares the complexity of x with the complexities of all strings of the same length, so that randomness can be defined with respect to M. The desired extension should preserve the intuition that if M has m elements, m is very large, and M can be described by a program whose length is negligible compared with log m, then almost all elements of M should have maximal complexity close to log m and therefore count as random with respect to M.

evidence.quote: The degree of randomness of a string x depends upon the complexity of the string x compared with the complexities of all strings having the same length. Extend this definition of randomness ‘with respect to an arbitrary finite set’. An appropriate solution should conform the following intuitive fact: if a finite set of strings M containing m elements, where m is very large, can be defined by a program of length negligible when compared with log m, then almost all elements of M should have maximal complexity (which is close to log m); these strings should be ‘random’ with respect to M. (C. Calude)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a binary string x, let C(x) denote its (plain or prefix-free) Kolmogorov complexity, i.e. the length of the shortest program (in a fixed universal Turing machine) that outputs x. For strings of length n, one classical measure of the "degree of randomness" of x compares C(x) with n = log|{0,1}^n|: x is considered (highly) random when C(x) is close to n. More generally, for a finite set M of strings, one can compare C(x) (or the conditional complexity C(x | M), given a description of M) with log|M|.

Problem. Define a notion of "degree of randomness of a string x with respect to an arbitrary finite set M of strings" that extends the usual notion (recovered when M = {0,1}^n) and that satisfies the following requirement: whenever M is a finite set of strings with |M| = m, m is very large, and M admits a program description whose length is negligible compared with log m, then almost every element x ∈ M should be assigned the maximal degree of randomness with respect to M, i.e. its complexity should be close to log m, so that almost all elements of M are "random with respect to M".

Provide such a definition and prove that it has the stated property.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a definitive resolution of this specific formulation (attributed to C. Calude) asking for a satisfactory notion of randomness of a string with respect to an arbitrary finite set. Related work exists on conditional Kolmogorov complexity, randomness deficiency relative to computable measures, and Kolmogorov's structure function, but no clearly identified solution to this exact problem was located. Status is therefore reported as unknown.
